label: Grinding on
summary: The world sits at 38, in the 'Bad' band, as two long emergencies pass grim milestones on the same day. The US struck Iran for a twelfth consecutive night, with CENTCOM saying the raids were meant to degrade Tehran's ability to threaten commercial shipping; Iranian media reported attacks on Bushehr, Ahvaz, Jask, Andimeshk and Sirik, and Khuzestan's deputy governor said two people were killed and eleven wounded at the Shalamcheh crossing with Iraq. Iran's health ministry now counts 53 dead and more than 590 injured since late June, eighteen American service members have died, and Iran's negotiator warned that 'if our security is not ensured, no infrastructure will be safe' while President Trump promised to destroy a bridge or power plant for every ship attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. Defense Secretary Hegseth told Congress the war has cost 37.5 billion dollars, nearly eight billion more than the last public figure, as Kuwait weighed electricity rationing after Iranian strikes on its power infrastructure and the Houthis declared Bab el-Mandeb closed to Saudi-bound vessels. In Africa, the Democratic Republic of Congo's Bundibugyo Ebola epidemic passed a thousand deaths — 1,031 fatalities among 2,473 confirmed cases in barely ten weeks, against eight months for the 2013-16 West African epidemic to reach the same mark — with Africa CDC's Jean Kaseya warning it could become the worst outbreak ever documented. Russia sent 216 Shahed-type and decoy drones plus four missiles at ten Ukrainian oblasts overnight; Israel's new 23-kilometre barrier now walls off the half of Gaza it controls, where an airstrike killed a family of six including four children; and India's exam-fraud protests deepened, with opposition MPs paralysing parliament after Rahul Gandhi's detention and the Supreme Court refusing to hear a petition on police violence. Tropical Storm Bertha came ashore in St Bernard Parish, Louisiana with 45 mph winds, pushing two to three feet of water along the Gulf and flooding roads around Houston. Against all that: three southern Lebanese villages began a phased Israeli withdrawal under the US-brokered framework, with the Lebanese army taking over and US carrier flights to Beirut set to resume after forty years; Cold Spring Harbor and Scripps researchers revived vancomycin against resistant bacteria; France became the third country to bar under-15s from social media; and Pacific ministers met in Sydney to coordinate ahead of COP31 as the ADB and Japan seeded a regional water-security fund. Markets barely moved, the S&P 500 easing 0.14 percent ahead of Big Tech earnings. The headline matches the rubric formula with no adjustment.

drivers.headline: The United States launches a twelfth consecutive night of strikes on Iran, with CENTCOM saying the raids aim to further degrade Tehran's ability to threaten civilian mariners and commercial vessels; Iranian media report attacks on Bushehr, Ahvaz, Jask, Andimeshk and Sirik, and Khuzestan's deputy governor says two people were killed and eleven wounded by a missile strike on the Shalamcheh border crossing with Iraq, while Iran's health ministry puts the toll since late June at 53 dead and more than 590 injured and Tehran's negotiator warns that 'if our security is not ensured, no infrastructure will be safe'

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth testifies that the US war on Iran has now cost 37.5 billion dollars, up nearly eight billion from the last public estimate, and asks Congress for tens of billions more for the Pentagon; Kuwait faces possible electricity rationing after Iranian strikes on its power infrastructure and on the Ali al-Salem airbase, Iran also hit US sites in Bahrain and Jordan, and Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich says Israel has 'no interest' in joining American operations

The Democratic Republic of the Congo's Bundibugyo Ebola epidemic passes a thousand deaths, with 1,031 fatalities among 2,473 confirmed cases and 737 people isolated or hospitalised barely ten weeks after the outbreak was declared on 15 May — the 2013-16 West African epidemic took eight months to reach the same toll — and there is no approved vaccine or treatment for this rarest of the four human Ebola strains; Africa CDC director-general Jean Kaseya warns that 'if we do not stop it today, this will become the worst outbreak the world has ever documented,' though Uganda discharged its last patient on 16 July, starting a 42-day countdown to being declared free of the virus

Russian forces fire one Iskander-M ballistic missile and three Kh-59/69 guided missiles from occupied Crimea along with 216 Shahed-type strike drones and Gerbera, Italmas and Parodiya decoys launched from Bryansk, Oryol, Millerovo, Primorsko-Akhtarsk and occupied Donetsk; Ukraine's air force downs three missiles and 204 drones, but one ballistic missile and twelve drones hit twelve locations, damaging residential, industrial and fuel infrastructure across Chernihiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Kharkiv, Kherson, Kyiv, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Sumy and Zaporizhia oblasts
drivers.source: Institute for the Study of War / Critical Threats

drivers.headline: The Israeli military is revealed to have built more than 23 kilometres of a giant barrier in recent months separating the portion of the Gaza Strip it controls — now just over half the territory — from the rest, hardening a de facto partition; an Israeli airstrike on Gaza City kills a family of six including four children, and more than 1,100 Palestinians have now been killed since the October ceasefire took effect

India's exam-fraud protests escalate into a constitutional standoff as opposition MPs, many dressed in black, disrupt both houses of parliament demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and forcing repeated suspensions, a day after police detained Congress leader Rahul Gandhi outside Prime Minister Modi's residence; the Supreme Court dismisses an urgent petition over police violence with Chief Justice Surya Kant telling counsel 'don't waste our time,' while 2.2 million medical students face retaking a leaked entrance exam, organisers say at least 150 protesters were wounded in Monday's march, and more than a dozen student suicides have been reported

Tropical Storm Bertha makes landfall near the Biloxi Wildlife Management Area in St Bernard Parish, Louisiana, about 40 miles east of New Orleans, with maximum sustained winds of 45 mph; a 63 mph gust is clocked at Venice, coastal inundation of two to three feet is measured from Pensacola westward with a peak rise of three feet at Shell Beach, and the storm's outer rain bands dump one to five inches on the Houston area, stranding cars in Sugar Land and closing roads near Highway 59 as the system tracks toward Texas

US stocks drift lower as rising oil prices weigh and investors wait on Tesla and Alphabet results, with the S&P 500 slipping 0.14 percent to 7,498.96, the Nasdaq Composite down 0.57 percent to 25,690.90 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average essentially flat, off 6.06 points or 0.01 percent at 52,218.58; indices remain near record territory but the Gulf shipping disruption keeps upward pressure on crude

Three villages in southern Lebanon begin implementing the phased withdrawal of Israeli forces under the framework agreement brokered between Israel, Lebanon and the United States, with the Lebanese army taking control of the vacated areas and overseeing Hezbollah's disarmament; residents of Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh wait for engineering units to clear explosive devices and unexploded ordnance before returning, and President Trump announces that direct US carrier flights to Lebanon will resume after a pause of more than forty years

Researchers at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory working with Scripps Research report that pairing vancomycin with a small molecule called pghi-4 — the first known inhibitor of the bacterial enzyme secreted antigen A — restores the last-resort antibiotic's ability to kill vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium, a result published in Nature Communications that suggests similar chemical partners could rescue other failing drugs, though the work remains preclinical with no timeline for human trials

Pacific governments close ranks on climate and security: environment ministers gather in Sydney for the sixth Pacific Climate Ministers Talanoa to coordinate positions ahead of COP31 in Türkiye, with Solomon Islands minister Wayne Ghemu calling regional solidarity 'a strategic necessity'; the Asian Development Bank and Japan launch the WISER water-security fund with an initial ten million dollars, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea sign a 2026-2029 defence cooperation statement of intent, and Fiji opens a 1.2 million dollar medical waste facility at Lautoka Hospital — even as Vanuatu declares meteorological drought across its northern provinces amid El Niño conditions

French lawmakers pass a bill banning social media accounts for children under 15 and prohibiting mobile phones for students in schools, making France the third country after Australia and the United Kingdom to legislate an age floor for social platforms, in a measure aimed at protecting adolescent mental health and classroom attention
